title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 9-11). Grothendieck is axiomatising a framework for 'tame' analysis situs, which he calls an 'atelier' (workshop). It consists of a set M of figures (closed tame pieces, 'multistrates') with four relations: ≤ (inclusion), ≪ (a subfigure relation; it is not plain set inclusion, and p.11 discusses how it should behave for simplices), ‖ (disjointness) and ≷ (compatibility, i.e. 'proper' or tame relative position). For figures X, Y, X̃ is the set of figures below X. K = X∩Y is defined as Sup{Z : Z ∈ X̃∩Ỹ}, the largest figure contained in both, which can differ from the naive set-theoretic intersection. X'_L = φ means that no non-empty subfigure of X' lies ≪ L, which by Cor. 4 on p.9 is equivalent to X' ‖ L.

Problem served. Page 9 states Propriété 2 ('special tubes'): if F and G become disjoint once one removes the common part L = F∩G, then F ≷ G. This page isolates the axiom needed for it.

At CD 2. Let X, Y ∈ M. Do not assume they are compatible, but form K = X∩Y. Suppose every X' ≪ X disjoint from K and every Y' ≪ Y disjoint from K satisfy X' ‖ Y'. In other words, away from their maximal common subfigure, X and Y do not meet. Then X ≷ Y. Grothendieck changes 'il suffit' to 'il faut', so the axiom is necessary for Propriété 2.

Where it fails. The axiom generally fails for polyhedral ateliers ('polyédraux'; the machine transcription reads 'polyidéaux'). These are characterised by: two compatible multistrates that are minimal (for inclusion) have a multistrate as intersection, i.e. X∩_F Y ∈ M is an inf in M. The reason is that in a polyhedral or simplicial world, compatibility requires meeting along a common face, which must itself belong to M.

At CD 2'. Same hypotheses as At CD 2, plus K ∈ M (K is an inf of X, Y in M). Then X ≷ Y. A crossed-out NB had said that each version implies At CD 1₀. The surviving NB says that every atelier he has in mind satisfies At CD 1₀ and, intuitively, one of At CD 2 or At CD 2'.

Moral drawn. The CD axioms reduce the compatibility relation ≷ between figures to the disjointness relation ‖. This shows the crucial role of disjointness, so ateliers should be built from (M, ≤, ≪, ‖_M) rather than from (M, ≤, ≪, ≷). A bottom-left margin warns that ‖ is not determined by (M, ≤, ≪_F); it must be given as extra data. Page 11 continues by asking for intrinsic axioms of special/polyhedral ateliers in terms of (M, ≤, ≪, ‖), and criticises the rigidity of affine simplices as the model for ≪.
errors: Notational slip: K is introduced as X∩Y, but the hypotheses are written with L (X'_L = φ_F, Y'_L = φ_F), carried over from p.9. L should read K.
Inconsistent subscripts: φ_F is used here, φ_𝓕 on p.9.

At CD 2' as written makes the hypothesis K ∈ M carry the whole difference from At CD 2. It is not shown that At CD 2' suffices for Propriété 2 restricted to polyhedral ateliers. The NB claiming that each version implies At CD 1₀ is crossed out, so the logical relations between the axioms are left unproved.

The definition of polyhedral ('polyédral') atelier is garbled by successive corrections: 'deux multistratifiés compatibles minimaux … ont pour intersection une multistrate'. It is unclear whether minimality is in M or among compatible pairs.

ideas.what: Axiom At CD 2: two figures whose only overlap is their maximal common subfigure K (they are disjoint away from K) are automatically compatible, i.e. in tame relative position.
ideas.modern_name: Tame intersection / relative position criterion, analogous to o-minimal or semialgebraic statements that a definable set meeting another only along a definable subset gives a definable pair (compatible stratifications)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (o-minimality, 1980s); Shiota (X-sets)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only calls for a 'topologie modérée' without such axioms

ideas.what: Variant At CD 2' for polyhedral ateliers: add the hypothesis that the intersection K is itself a figure (an inf in M). Polyhedral ateliers are characterised by minimal compatible multistrates having an intersection in M.
ideas.modern_name: Face-intersection condition of simplicial/polyhedral complexes, recast as a lattice-theoretic (existence of inf) axiom

ideas.what: Methodological claim: in a tame-topology axiomatics, compatibility (≷) should be derived from a primitive disjointness relation ‖, which is not determined by inclusion and the subfigure relation. The atelier is then a structure (M, ≤, ≪, ‖).
ideas.modern_name: Point-free / mereotopological axiomatics (part-of, well-inside, disjoint/contact relations); proximity and contact algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna (1920s), de Vries (1962), Efremovich (proximity spaces), region connection calculus

missed.claim: A point-free axiomatics of tame topology. The 'atelier' is a structure (M, ≤, ≪, ‖) of figures with a disjointness relation, in which compatibility is defined from disjointness via the CD axioms. It is split into variants (special vs polyhedral ateliers), and the program of finding intrinsic axioms in terms of (M, ≤, ≪, ‖) is explicitly left open (p.11).
missed.quote: le rôle crucial de cette notion de disjonction dans la construction d'ateliers ; … ou maintenant en termes de (M, ≤, ≪, ‖_M)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: No published axiomatisation of Grothendieck's tame topology exists. These notes give concrete candidate axioms that could be tested against o-minimal structures, PL, or subanalytic categories.

missed.claim: The structure (figures, inclusion, a well-inside relation ≪, disjointness ‖) and statements like Cor. 3 (disjointness inherited by ≪-smaller pieces) closely parallel mereotopology and contact/proximity algebras. Grothendieck's motivation, however, is tame/stratified geometry. A link between de Vries/contact-algebra style point-free topology and o-minimal/tame topology via Grothendieck's ateliers seems absent from the literature.
missed.quote: At CD, c'est de nouveau la relation d'intersection ≷ dans M … à la propriété ‖
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a lattice-theoretic or point-free foundation for tame geometry, bridging logic-based o-minimality and algebraic point-free topology.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, fairly concrete fragment of Grothendieck's tame-topology ('ateliers') axiomatics, centred on reducing compatibility to disjointness. It is interesting as a record of his program, but it consists of axiom-tuning rather than a finished result, and its ideas are close to standard PL and o-minimal intuitions.
transcription_corrections: 'ateliers dits "polyidéaux"' should almost certainly read 'polyédraux' (polyhedral), consistent with p.11 ('ateliers spéciaux ou polyédraux'). Likewise the margin of At CD 2' should read 'ateliers polyédraux'.
Line 2: 'Soient X, Y_{≠} ∈ M, [-tq-] on suppose pas X, Y [?] compatibles' reads 'Soient X, Y ∈ M, ~~tq~~ on ne suppose pas X ≷ Y compatibles mais on introduit K = X∩Y = Sup_{Z∈X̃∩Ỹ} Z'.
Line 1: 'il suffit' is overwritten by 'il faut' ('Pour ceci, il faut qu'on ait l'axiome suivant').

Final paragraph is roughly: 'At CD, c'est de nouveau [ramener] la relation d'intersection ≷ dans M … à la propriété ‖ dans M, ce qui montre le rôle crucial de cette notion de disjonction dans la construction d'ateliers à partir de (M, ≤, ≪, …), ou maintenant en termes de (M, ≤, ≪, ‖_M)'.
Bottom-left margin begins 'Attention la relation ‖ dans M ne résulte pas de la donnée de (M, ≤, ≪_F) …'.
